title: Complete the square with a negative middle term

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: Write x^2 - 4x + 1 in the form (x + a)^2 + b.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The middle term is -4x, so the bracket should be (x - 2), not (x + 2).
(x - 2)^2 gives +4, so to end at +1 you need -3 outside.

hint_ladder.title: What sign should be inside the square?
hint_ladder.prompt: The sign of the middle term controls the sign inside the completed square bracket.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Halve the coefficient of x while keeping its sign, then build the squared bracket from that value.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Check both the size and the negative sign, then check the direction of the outside constant adjustment.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For x^2 + bx + c, build (x + b/2)^2 and then compare its constant with the original constant. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.action: halve the x coefficient with sign
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is preserving the negative sign when halving the middle coefficient.
The stuck point is adjusting the constant in the correct direction.

mark_scheme_notes: Award credit for (x-2)^2 and correct -3 adjustment.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: sign loss and wrong constant adjustment direction.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how will you keep track of the negative sign?
